Features: Pre-built UI components (SignIn, SignUp, UserButton, UserProfile), sessions, MFA, passkeys, social login (Google, GitHub, etc.), organization/multi-tenant support, user management dashboard, webhook events, extensive SDKs (React, Next.js, vanilla JS, mobile).
Pricing Model: Free tier: 10,000 MAUs. Paid: $0.02/MAU after free tier (plans scale with features — Pro, Business, Enterprise add SSO, custom roles, advanced MFA). Transparent pricing.
Integration Complexity: Low — install SDK, wrap app in ClerkProvider, add pre-built components or use hooks. ~30-45 min to basic setup.
Best For: Most apps that want fast setup with pre-built UI — SaaS, dashboards, marketplaces, any app that wants login fast without building auth UI.
MFA: Built-in (TOTP, SMS, email — on paid plans).
Hosted UI: Yes — pre-built SignIn, SignUp, UserButton, UserProfile components.

Features: Flexible auth with many providers (Google, GitHub, Twitter, etc.), email/password, magic links, sessions (database or JWT), callbacks, adapters for many databases/ORMs, well-established ecosystem.
Pricing Model: Free — you pay only for your own infrastructure (database, hosting). No per-user fees. You manage the server.
Integration Complexity: Medium — more setup than Clerk: configure providers, set up database adapter, handle callbacks, build your own sign-in UI or use minimal pre-built pages. More control, more work.
Best For: Apps that want full control, lowest cost, self-hosted, no vendor lock-in — custom apps, apps with specific auth flows, budget-conscious projects.
Default For: When you want full control + lowest cost, or self-hosted auth.
MFA: You implement it (TOTP via otplib, etc.).
SSO: You implement it (via integration with SSO providers).
Hosted UI: Minimal — you build your own UI or use basic pre-built pages.

Features: Broad provider support, SSO (SAML, OIDC, WS-Fed), MFA, passwordless, anomaly detection, breach detection, user management, roles/permissions, rules/actions (serverless functions for custom logic), extensive enterprise features, compliance certifications (SOC2, HIPAA, ISO, GDPR, etc.).
Pricing Model: Free tier: 7,500 MAUs. Paid tiers scale with MAUs and features — Essentials, Plus, Enterprise. Can be expensive at scale. Custom pricing for enterprise.
Integration Complexity: Medium — install SDK, configure application in Auth0 dashboard, set up callbacks, handle authentication events. Enterprise features add complexity.
Best For: Enterprise apps needing SSO, compliance-heavy apps (healthcare, finance, regulated industries), apps needing advanced security features, apps with complex identity requirements.
MFA: Built-in (TOTP, SMS, email, push, WebAuthn, custom MFA policies).
SSO: Built-in (SAML, OIDC, WS-Fed — extensive SSO support).

Features: Email/password, magic links, social login (Google, GitHub, etc.), phone auth (via Twilio), MFA (TOTP), user management via REST API/Realtime, integrates with Supabase database (user metadata in postgres), JWT sessions, row-level security (RLS) integration.
Pricing Model: Free tier: 50,000 MAUs (with some limits). Paid: Pro $25/month (500k MAUs +), then usage-based. Affordable for small-to-medium apps.
Integration Complexity: Low-Medium — use Supabase JS SDK, configure auth in Supabase dashboard, handle sign-in/sign-up flows. Integrates naturally if using Supabase for database too.
Best For: Apps using Supabase for database that want auth in the same ecosystem, apps wanting a simple managed auth with PostgreSQL backing.
SSO: Not built-in (would need external SSO integration).

Features: Email/password, magic links, phone auth (SMS), social login (Google, Facebook, GitHub, etc.), federated identity, anonymous auth, multi-factor auth (SMS, TOTP), user management via Admin SDK, integrates with Firebase ecosystem (Firestore, Storage, Analytics).
Pricing Model: Free tier: generous (10k phone auth verifications/month, etc.). Paid: Blaze plan — pay-as-you-go beyond free limits. Phone auth can get expensive.
Integration Complexity: Low — use Firebase JS SDK, configure in Firebase console, handle sign-in flows. Very easy to start.
Best For: Mobile-first apps, apps already using Firebase, apps wanting real-time + auth + storage in one ecosystem.
SSO: Not built-in (would need external SSO integration).

Features: Lightweight, framework-agnostic session/auth library. You define the user model and session model. Works with any database/ORM. Gives you full control over auth flow, session storage, validation. Supports cookie-based sessions, database-backed sessions.
Pricing Model: Free — open source. You pay only for infrastructure (database, hosting).
Integration Complexity: Medium-High — you build the auth flow: sign-up, sign-in, password hashing, session creation/validation, cookies, logout. More work than Clerk/NextAuth, but full control and no hidden complexity.
Best For: Apps wanting custom session-based auth with full control, lightweight apps, apps where you want to own the auth implementation but don't want to build everything from scratch.
Default For: When you want custom auth with full control but don't want to build everything from scratch.
Hosted UI: No — you build your own UI.

Features: Full control. You build everything: password hashing (bcrypt/argon2id), session management (httpOnly cookies or JWT), sign-up/sign-in flows, token generation/validation, session storage, expiry, refresh, logout, password reset, email verification, MFA (if you want it).
Pricing Model: Free — open source components, you pay for infrastructure. But the hidden cost is development time, security review, ongoing maintenance.
Integration Complexity: High — you build everything. Requires deep understanding of auth security: password hashing, session management, CSRF, timing attacks, token security, cookie security, password reset flows, email verification, MFA. High risk of getting it wrong if you're not experienced.
Best For: Apps where you need absolute control and have the expertise to implement auth securely. Rarely the right choice for a team without auth expertise.
Default For: Only when you have auth expertise and absolutely need custom auth. Rarely recommended for small teams.
